## 🎯 Learning Objectives

By the end of this lesson you will be able to:

- Use Android Studio's ML Model Binding to auto-generate inference code
- Profile CPU, memory, and GPU usage during AI inference
- Use the System Trace to identify inference bottlenecks
- Add custom trace markers to your inference pipeline
- Read and interpret profiler flame graphs for AI workloads

---

## 1. ML Model Binding — Auto-Generated Kotlin Code

Android Studio can import a `.tflite` file and generate type-safe Kotlin wrapper code automatically:

```
Steps:
1. Right-click app/src/main/ → New → Other → TensorFlow Lite Model
2. Select your .tflite file
3. Android Studio generates:
   - A Kotlin data class matching the model's inputs/outputs
   - Type-safe inference methods
   - Automatic preprocessing helpers

Result: Zero-boilerplate TFLite inference
```

### What Gets Generated

After importing `mobilenetv2.tflite`, Android Studio generates:

```kotlin
// Auto-generated: app/src/main/ml/Mobilenetv2.kt
// DO NOT EDIT — regenerated when model changes

package com.yourname.benchmark.ml

import android.content.Context
import android.graphics.Bitmap
import org.tensorflow.lite.DataType
import org.tensorflow.lite.support.image.ImageProcessor
import org.tensorflow.lite.support.image.TensorImage
import org.tensorflow.lite.support.image.ops.ResizeOp
import org.tensorflow.lite.support.model.Model
import org.tensorflow.lite.support.tensorbuffer.TensorBuffer

class Mobilenetv2 private constructor(
    private val model: Model
) {
    companion object {
        // Default factory — uses CPU
        fun newInstance(context: Context) = Mobilenetv2(
            Model.createModel(context, "mobilenetv2.tflite")
        )

        // Factory with custom options (GPU, NNAPI, etc.)
        fun newInstance(context: Context, options: Model.Options) = Mobilenetv2(
            Model.createModel(context, "mobilenetv2.tflite", options)
        )
    }

    // Auto-generated Outputs class matching model output tensor
    data class Outputs(
        val probabilityAsTensorBuffer: TensorBuffer
    ) {
        // Convenience: get float array directly
        val probabilityList: List<Float>
            get() = probabilityAsTensorBuffer.floatArray.toList()
    }

    // Type-safe process method
    fun process(tensorImage: TensorImage): Outputs {
        val outputFeature0 = TensorBuffer.createFixedSize(
            intArrayOf(1, 1000), DataType.FLOAT32
        )
        model.run(arrayOf(tensorImage.buffer), mapOf(0 to outputFeature0.buffer))
        return Outputs(probabilityAsTensorBuffer = outputFeature0)
    }

    fun close() = model.close()
}
```

### Using the Generated Code

```kotlin
// Extremely clean inference — no boilerplate
class ClassifierWithBinding(context: Context) {

    // With GPU acceleration
    private val model = Mobilenetv2.newInstance(
        context,
        Model.Options.Builder()
            .setDevice(Model.Device.GPU)     // GPU
            // .setDevice(Model.Device.NNAPI) // or NNAPI
            // .setDevice(Model.Device.CPU)   // or CPU
            .setNumThreads(4)
            .build()
    )

    private val imageProcessor = ImageProcessor.Builder()
        .add(ResizeOp(224, 224, ResizeOp.ResizeMethod.BILINEAR))
        .build()

    fun classify(bitmap: Bitmap): List<Float> {
        val image   = imageProcessor.process(TensorImage.fromBitmap(bitmap))
        val outputs = model.process(image)
        return outputs.probabilityList
    }

    fun close() = model.close()
}
```

## 2. Android Studio Profiler Overview

The Android Studio Profiler has 4 tabs — all useful for AI debugging:

```
Profiler
├── CPU Profiler       ← how much CPU your inference uses, method traces
├── Memory Profiler    ← heap usage, GC events, native allocations
├── Energy Profiler    ← battery drain from your AI workload
└── Network Profiler   ← (not relevant for on-device AI)
```

**How to open:**
```
Android Studio → View → Tool Windows → Profiler
Select your running process from the dropdown
```

---

## 3. CPU Profiler — Find Inference Bottlenecks

### Step 1: Record a CPU Trace

```
Profiler → CPU tab → Record → [run your AI inference] → Stop recording
Select "System Trace" for native code profiling (TFLite is native C++)
```

### Step 2: Add Custom Trace Markers

Mark your inference stages so they appear in the trace:

```kotlin
// InferenceTracer.kt
package com.yourname.benchmark

import android.os.Trace

/**
 * Wrapper that adds Android System Trace markers around inference stages.
 * These appear as colored blocks in the CPU Profiler → System Trace view.
 */
object InferenceTracer {

    /**
     * Trace a block of code. Shows up as a colored section in Systrace.
     * Use for: preprocessing, inference, postprocessing
     */
    inline fun <T> trace(sectionName: String, block: () -> T): T {
        Trace.beginSection(sectionName)
        return try {
            block()
        } finally {
            Trace.endSection()
        }
    }
}

// Usage in your inference pipeline:
class TracedClassifier(context: Context) {

    private val model = Mobilenetv2.newInstance(context)
    private val imageProcessor = ImageProcessor.Builder()
        .add(ResizeOp(224, 224, ResizeOp.ResizeMethod.BILINEAR))
        .build()

    fun classify(bitmap: Bitmap): List<Float> {

        // Each of these appears as a named block in the profiler timeline
        val image = InferenceTracer.trace("Preprocess_Image") {
            imageProcessor.process(TensorImage.fromBitmap(bitmap))
        }

        val outputs = InferenceTracer.trace("TFLite_Inference") {
            model.process(image)
        }

        return InferenceTracer.trace("Decode_Output") {
            outputs.probabilityList
                .mapIndexed { idx, score -> idx to score }
                .sortedByDescending { it.second }
                .take(5)
                .map { it.second }
        }
    }

    fun close() = model.close()
}
```

### Step 3: Reading the Flame Graph

```
System Trace view shows:
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ Thread: main                                         │
  │  ├─ analyze() ████████████████████████████ 45ms     │
  │  │   ├─ Preprocess_Image ████ 8ms                   │
  │  │   ├─ TFLite_Inference ████████████████ 30ms      │
  │  │   └─ Decode_Output ██ 7ms                        │
  │                                                      │
  │ Thread: TFLite_Worker (background thread)            │
  │  └─ [GPU Delegate ops running here]                  │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Reading the flame graph:
  Wide block   = long duration (likely bottleneck)
  Deep stack   = many nested calls (may indicate inefficiency)
  Red blocks   = jank or dropped frames
  Your sections = named by Trace.beginSection()
```

## 4. Memory Profiler — Track AI Memory Usage

### Monitor Model Loading Memory

```kotlin
// MemoryProfiler.kt
package com.yourname.benchmark

import android.os.Debug
import android.util.Log

object MemoryProfiler {

    private const val TAG = "MemoryProfiler"

    data class MemorySnapshot(
        val javaHeapMb: Float,
        val nativeHeapMb: Float,
        val totalPss: Float,
        val label: String
    )

    /**
     * Take a memory snapshot and log it.
     * Call before and after model loading to measure impact.
     */
    fun snapshot(label: String): MemorySnapshot {
        val javaHeap   = Debug.getNativeHeapAllocatedSize() / (1024f * 1024f)
        val nativeHeap = (Runtime.getRuntime().totalMemory() -
                          Runtime.getRuntime().freeMemory()) / (1024f * 1024f)

        val memInfo = Debug.MemoryInfo()
        Debug.getMemoryInfo(memInfo)
        val totalPss = memInfo.totalPss / 1024f

        val snapshot = MemorySnapshot(javaHeap, nativeHeap, totalPss, label)

        Log.d(TAG, "[$label] " +
            "Java heap: ${javaHeap.toInt()} MB  " +
            "Native: ${nativeHeap.toInt()} MB  " +
            "Total PSS: ${totalPss.toInt()} MB"
        )

        return snapshot
    }

    /**
     * Profile model loading — shows exactly how much RAM the model uses.
     */
    suspend fun profileModelLoad(loadBlock: suspend () -> Unit): Pair<MemorySnapshot, MemorySnapshot> {
        System.gc()  // clean up before measuring
        val before = snapshot("Before model load")
        loadBlock()
        val after = snapshot("After model load")

        val delta = after.nativeHeapMb - before.nativeHeapMb
        Log.d(TAG, "Model memory footprint: ${delta.toInt()} MB")

        return before to after
    }
}
```

### Usage

```kotlin
// Profile exact memory usage of your model
lifecycleScope.launch(Dispatchers.IO) {
    MemoryProfiler.profileModelLoad {
        classifier = Mobilenetv2.newInstance(context,
            Model.Options.Builder().setDevice(Model.Device.GPU).build()
        )
    }
}

// Output example:
// [Before model load] Java heap: 45 MB  Native: 120 MB  Total PSS: 210 MB
// [After model load]  Java heap: 45 MB  Native: 260 MB  Total PSS: 355 MB
// Model memory footprint: 140 MB
```

## 5. Energy Profiler — Measure Battery Impact

```kotlin
// EnergyAwareInference.kt
package com.yourname.benchmark

import android.os.PowerManager
import android.util.Log

/**
 * Monitor device thermal state during inference.
 * Prevents thermal throttling by backing off when device gets hot.
 */
class ThermalAwareInference(context: Context) {

    private val powerManager = context.getSystemService(PowerManager::class.java)
    private var consecutiveInferences = 0

    companion object {
        private const val TAG = "ThermalAware"
        private const val THERMAL_COOLDOWN_INTERVAL = 50   // cool down every N inferences
        private const val COOLDOWN_DELAY_MS = 100L
    }

    /**
     * Run inference with thermal awareness.
     * Automatically inserts cooldown pauses when device thermal status is elevated.
     */
    suspend fun runWithThermalCheck(inferenceBlock: suspend () -> Unit) {
        consecutiveInferences++

        // Check thermal status (Android 10+)
        val thermalStatus = powerManager?.currentThermalStatus
            ?: PowerManager.THERMAL_STATUS_NONE

        when {
            thermalStatus >= PowerManager.THERMAL_STATUS_SEVERE -> {
                Log.w(TAG, "⚠️ SEVERE thermal — pausing inference")
                kotlinx.coroutines.delay(500L)
            }
            thermalStatus >= PowerManager.THERMAL_STATUS_MODERATE -> {
                Log.d(TAG, "Moderate thermal — brief pause")
                kotlinx.coroutines.delay(COOLDOWN_DELAY_MS)
            }
            consecutiveInferences % THERMAL_COOLDOWN_INTERVAL == 0 -> {
                // Proactive cooldown every N inferences (for real-time video)
                kotlinx.coroutines.delay(16L)  // 1 frame worth of breathing room
            }
        }

        inferenceBlock()
    }

    /**
     * Get current thermal status as a human-readable string.
     */
    fun getThermalStatus(): String {
        val status = powerManager?.currentThermalStatus ?: return "Unknown"
        return when (status) {
            PowerManager.THERMAL_STATUS_NONE      -> "✅ Normal"
            PowerManager.THERMAL_STATUS_LIGHT     -> "🟡 Light"
            PowerManager.THERMAL_STATUS_MODERATE  -> "🟠 Moderate"
            PowerManager.THERMAL_STATUS_SEVERE    -> "🔴 Severe"
            PowerManager.THERMAL_STATUS_CRITICAL  -> "🚨 Critical"
            PowerManager.THERMAL_STATUS_EMERGENCY -> "⛔ Emergency"
            PowerManager.THERMAL_STATUS_SHUTDOWN  -> "💀 Shutdown imminent"
            else -> "Unknown ($status)"
        }
    }
}
```

## 6. Systrace — Full System View

For deep performance analysis, use Android's Systrace:

```bash
# Capture a systrace while running inference
adb shell atrace --async_start -a com.yourname.benchmark \
  -c gfx input view dalvik camera audio hal res

# Run your inference in the app for 10 seconds

# Stop and pull trace
adb shell atrace --async_stop -o /data/local/tmp/trace.html
adb pull /data/local/tmp/trace.html ./trace.html

# Open trace.html in Chrome browser
# Look for:
#   - Your Trace.beginSection() markers
#   - "TFLite" entries in the timeline
#   - GPU workload in the "GPU Counter" row
#   - CPU frequency scaling during inference
```

## 7. InferenceProfiler.kt — Complete Profiling Utility

```kotlin
// InferenceProfiler.kt
package com.yourname.benchmark

import android.os.SystemClock
import android.os.Trace
import android.util.Log
import kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers
import kotlinx.coroutines.withContext

data class InferenceProfile(
    val modelName: String,
    val backend: String,
    val avgLatencyMs: Float,
    val minLatencyMs: Long,
    val maxLatencyMs: Long,
    val p95LatencyMs: Long,
    val avgMemoryMb: Float,
    val runsCompleted: Int
)

object InferenceProfiler {

    private const val TAG = "InferenceProfiler"

    /**
     * Profile an inference function over multiple runs.
     * Returns detailed statistics.
     */
    suspend fun profile(
        modelName: String,
        backend: String,
        warmupRuns: Int = 5,
        timedRuns: Int = 20,
        inferenceBlock: suspend () -> Unit
    ): InferenceProfile = withContext(Dispatchers.Default) {

        Log.d(TAG, "Profiling: $modelName on $backend ($warmupRuns warmup, $timedRuns timed)")

        // Warmup — let JIT and shader caches stabilize
        Trace.beginSection("Warmup_$modelName")
        repeat(warmupRuns) {
            try { inferenceBlock() } catch (e: Exception) { /* ignore warmup errors */ }
        }
        Trace.endSection()

        // Timed runs
        val latencies = mutableListOf<Long>()

        Trace.beginSection("Profile_$modelName")
        repeat(timedRuns) { run ->
            val start = SystemClock.elapsedRealtimeNanos()
            inferenceBlock()
            val elapsed = (SystemClock.elapsedRealtimeNanos() - start) / 1_000_000

            latencies.add(elapsed)
            Log.v(TAG, "  Run $run: ${elapsed}ms")
        }
        Trace.endSection()

        // Calculate statistics
        latencies.sort()
        val avg = latencies.average().toFloat()
        val min = latencies.first()
        val max = latencies.last()
        val p95 = latencies[(latencies.size * 0.95).toInt()]

        // Memory snapshot
        val memMb = Debug.getNativeHeapAllocatedSize() / (1024f * 1024f)

        val profile = InferenceProfile(
            modelName     = modelName,
            backend       = backend,
            avgLatencyMs  = avg,
            minLatencyMs  = min,
            maxLatencyMs  = max,
            p95LatencyMs  = p95,
            avgMemoryMb   = memMb,
            runsCompleted = timedRuns
        )

        logProfile(profile)
        profile
    }

    private fun logProfile(p: InferenceProfile) {
        Log.d(TAG, """
            ═══════════════════════════════════
            Model  : ${p.modelName}
            Backend: ${p.backend}
            ───────────────────────────────────
            Avg    : ${p.avgLatencyMs.toInt()}ms
            Min    : ${p.minLatencyMs}ms
            Max    : ${p.maxLatencyMs}ms
            P95    : ${p.p95LatencyMs}ms
            Memory : ${p.avgMemoryMb.toInt()} MB native
            ═══════════════════════════════════
        """.trimIndent())
    }

    /**
     * Format a list of profiles into a markdown-style comparison table.
     */
    fun formatComparisonTable(profiles: List<InferenceProfile>): String {
        val sb = StringBuilder()
        sb.appendLine("| Backend | Avg (ms) | Min | Max | P95 |")
        sb.appendLine("|---|---|---|---|---|")
        profiles.forEach { p ->
            sb.appendLine(
                "| ${p.backend} | ${p.avgLatencyMs.toInt()} " +
                "| ${p.minLatencyMs} | ${p.maxLatencyMs} | ${p.p95LatencyMs} |"
            )
        }
        return sb.toString()
    }
}
```

## 8. Profiling Checklist

```
Before profiling:
  □ Enable USB debugging on device
  □ Keep device plugged in (battery level affects CPU/GPU frequency)
  □ Close background apps (minimize RAM/CPU competition)
  □ Disable screen auto-rotate during profiling
  □ Warm up for 5+ runs before timing

During profiling:
  □ Use SystemClock.elapsedRealtimeNanos() not System.currentTimeMillis()
  □ Add Trace.beginSection() markers for each pipeline stage
  □ Record at least 20 runs for stable averages
  □ Check both avg AND p95 latency (p95 is what users experience on slow runs)

After profiling:
  □ Check if inference is on the right thread (background, not main)
  □ Verify GPU/NNAPI is actually being used (check logcat)
  □ Profile with Systrace to see full system picture
  □ Test on multiple device tiers (budget, mid-range, flagship)
```

---

## 9. Summary

- ML Model Binding generates type-safe Kotlin wrappers — zero boilerplate inference code
- `Trace.beginSection()` / `endSection()` adds named blocks to System Trace profiler
- `MemoryProfiler.profileModelLoad()` measures exact RAM footprint of model loading
- `ThermalAwareInference` prevents performance degradation from thermal throttling
- Always use `SystemClock.elapsedRealtimeNanos()` for accurate timing — not `System.currentTimeMillis()`
- Profile both avg and P95 latency — avg hides occasional slow runs that users notice
- Systrace gives the full picture: CPU frequency, GPU usage, JVM GC events, all in one view
